correctness.rationale: PASS applies to repairs/5/RESULT.md, not the original shortcut. The frozen Finding and proof omit a≡4 (mod 7) from the cases with F=P_a(a−2). At a=11 the verified PF set is {72,111,112}, so the frozen shortcut gives 111 instead of 112. The original PF table itself is correct. Re-audit of the repair: the 1,3 minimum H increases by 1 or 3 on adding 7, which proves greedy optimality with seven-coins and the periodic λ. For a residue −m the offset m suffices and all larger congruent offsets cost more than the unit-coin bound, hence W_a(m) is the exact Apéry representative. Earlier indices cannot dominate later ones because any possible backward gain is at most 2, below the multiplicity. A later index dominates an earlier one exactly when the coin count is additive at their offset difference, which is equivalent to the existence of a first coin step staying below a and raising λ by one. The seven-step restricts the last seven positions, and the unit and three-step residue increments give precisely J_r. For the separate numerical maximum, W(m+7)−W(m)=8a−7, and any suffix to a−1 containing a positive step has positive total increment because each negative run has length at most two. Hence j_F is the length of the terminal negative run, giving offsets (1,2,0,0,1,0,0). Each non-a generator is the Apéry member of its own coin offset and has only its one-coin presentation at minimum value, so the four are minimal. Independent exact residue-graph and generator-membership checks for all 493 parameters 8≤a≤500 confirmed the PF table and corrected Frobenius offsets; replay: branches/f1a4b85c-c28d-40ff-b434-61b3481dc1cc/record5_independent_check.py and record5_independent_8_500.txt.
